ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within a grid of small squares with side length $1$, points $A, B, C, D$ are all at the vertices of these small squares. Lines $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at point $O$. What is the value of $\cos\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $CE$ and $DE$ as shown in the figure:\\
Since it is known from the figure that $\angle 1=\angle 2=\angle 3=\angle 4=\angle ABE=45^\circ$\\
Thus, $\angle CED=\angle 2+\angle 3=90^\circ$, $AB\parallel CE$\\
Therefore, $\angle BOD=\angle DCE$\\
Since the side length of the small square is $1$\\
Therefore, in $Rt\triangle CDE$, $CE=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$, $CD=\sqrt{1^2+3^2}=\sqrt{10}$\\
Therefore, $\cos\angle DCE=\frac{CE}{CD}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}$\\
Therefore, $\cos\angle BOD=\cos\angle DCE=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

Therefore, $\angle BOD=\angle DCE$\\
Since the side length of the small square is $1$\\
Therefore, in $Rt\triangle CDE$, $CE=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$, $CD=\sqrt{1^2+3^2}=\sqrt{10}$\\
Therefore, $\cos\angle DCE=\frac{CE}{CD}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}$\\
Therefore, $\cos\angle BOD=\cos\angle DCE=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}$
